name: security-cors-preflight-lifecycle-review
intent: Preflight caching and credentialed CORS across an actual policy transition
artifacts: OPTIONS and actual response traces, credential mode, origin allowlist, Vary/cache behavior and policy transition fixture.
trace: Determine which decision is cached by the browser and which remains enforced on the actual response/server operation. Track method/header/origin and profile identity.
experiment: In an owned fixture compare fresh and previously preflighted contexts before and after narrowing permission; observe actual browser reads and committed synthetic effects.
disproof: A cached successful OPTIONS response does not alone expose a credentialed body or authorize a state change.
repair: Enforce the actual request/response boundary and retest both cached and fresh browser paths.
branch_decisions: Classify browser-readable protected data separately from a cookie-authenticated mutation. The browser preflight cache differs from an HTTP response cache; simple requests need no preflight. Actual credentials and SameSite admission still matter. Cached preflight permission does not remove response CORS checks; if only a PUT commits, investigate server authorization/CSRF and compare fresh, cached and expired states.
